When a mutating admission controller changes managedFields in a way that causes them to be invalid, this change will reset them to their state before the admission chain modified them.

Conformance test fail specifically on admission webhooks, that might be related ;-)
bazel-test fails on endpoint, I haven't looked but I'm sure you've changed something there.

issue_context.title: [Server-Side Apply] Prevent mutating admission controllers from corrupting managedFields
issue_context.body:
This issue is meant as a space for discussing mutating webhooks regarding Server-Side Apply.

Primarily the problem recently reported in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/96351.
As discovered in the issue it is possible for a mutating admission webhook to change the managedFields in a way that would break apply.

This can be "achieved" accidentally by running a webhook with an outdated version of client-go that doesn't understand managedFields yet.

In the specific case it seemed like the webhook did not know about managedFields and as a result computed a patch to remove them. The exact process is not clear yet, as we don't have access to the specific webhook.

In general, we should make it impossible to set invalid managedFields in the admission chain.

We have a few options to do that:
1. Validate managedFields after the admission chain and reset them to the state before admission on invalid fields.
  This would hide an error like an outdated admission hook. Right now we still have the chance to not hide errors, before going GA.
2. Validate managedFields after the admission chain and fail the request on invalid fields.
  Failing the request directly would break the user for something they can't directly fix and might need a Cluster-Admin for.
3. Validate managedFields after every admission controller and return an error to the controller on invalid fields.
  This might be better than failing the request itself, as the request could still succeed depending on the failure policy of the webhook.
4. [Track managedFields for admission controllers](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/1085) and overwrite changes done to them in the admission chain.
  It's still open for discussion if admission controllers should be able to change managedFields.
  If not, tracking their changes directly should be the goal eventually.
5. Always reset managed fields after mutation, i.e. discard any changes made by mutation, what-so-ever.

/sig api-machinery
/wg api-expression
/cc @apelisse
comments: I think one option that you possibly missed: Always reset managed fields after mutation, i.e. discard any changes made by mutation, what-so-ever.
Added, might be a small step towards 4. as we "fix" or workaround the error until we can track mutations.

Let me attempt to split this issue into a couple separate dimensions, which are not strictly orthogonal:
1. Do we want to track fields changed by admission-chain, and give them their own "managedfields"
   a. If we have managedFields for admission-chain, is there a relationship between the admission-change and the request that initiated the change or not?
2. Do we want to allow admission-chain to alter managedFields?
  a. If we do so, should we fail the request when the managedFields is corrupted
  b. If we don't, should we reject the request when they try

The problem in this issue is mostly related to that "2." I think.

review_comments:
Yes, but somewhat unrelated, shouldn't we do something useful if the managedfields is invalid here?

Should we replace `emptyManagedFieldsOnErr` method with a `decodeManagedFieldsOrEmpty`, which could be used here?

Shouldn't we keep returning the error here if decoding fails (it is apply)?
What would we want to happen if live is corrupted?
It could only happen if somebody updates it and then applies would fail in the future.  I'd say we then should prevent invalid managedFields from getting persisted, what this PR tries to at least make harder.
Right, if the managed fields are corrupted in the apiserver, then someone can't apply anymore. The right thing to do is to restart fresh I would say.
I haven't look at `internal` yet, but can we get rid of the indirection here? I'd rather avoid having too many "DecodeManagedFields" functions if possible :-)

I looked at it for a bit, but I didn't want to move too much outside the internal package if not needed.
There are a few internal types and decoding functions right now, but in theory we could move everything I think.
We would be splitting up decoding and encoding though, or move encoding as well. But I'm not sure if I want to also expose encoding.
Have a look and tell me what you think, I can do it either way.

I moved this part in here as a first step to consolidate managedFields validation.
The function was always only called next to ValidateFieldManager so it shouldn't make a difference (except of looping over managedFields one time less).

A very basic test for checking the admission controller actually resets.
Not sure if we need more in combination with the validation tests we already have.
This always returns nil error, does it need to return that?

Yeah, I made it this way for ease of use so it can just wrap the function call for providing the same return values.
So no additional error check or anything is required.
I hope you don't mind be borrowing that burger here, just to test the fieldManager code gets called.

we could send a warning here as well.
like `".metadata.managedFields failed to decode; using managedFields from live object instead"`
